broken.item: B-amber-followup regression (item 4 class, the literal ' for ' join) — still present when nothing follows the first part after 'payroll'
broken.why: Repro on the current tree (stub run, both the ppl fixture and the test file's Payai fixture): 'Run Retail payroll for End-Month staff', 'Run the Retail payroll for End-Month employees', '... for End-Month workers', '... for End-Month people', '... for our End-Month team', '... for the End-Month crew', 'Run the Retail payroll for the Retail team', '... for the store team', 'Run Retail payroll for the End-Month one', and 'Run Payai Retail payroll for End-Month staff'. At HEAD each one asks the scheme question (Retail End-Month / Retail Mid-Month). Now each is refused: 'I could not find "End-Month staff" among the people this scheme pays.' Cause: actions_amber.py, in the final else of _period_words_to_scheme (around lines 575-597). When the scheme slot has no cut (tail == '') and said+head do not cover exactly one scheme, it still falls through to texts['scheme'] = '%s for %s', and _split_people then cuts the words after 'payroll' off as people. Smallest fix that matches the convergence rule: in that last branch, only join with ' for ' when there is a tail or `head` names somebody (_names_somebody). Otherwise leave texts as they came in (HEAD behaviour) or join with a space. The Warehouse pin is not affected, because it goes through the month-phrase elif branch.

broken.item: B-amber-followup regression (items 2/3 class, non-month words moved into the scheme): Vietnamese filler words that are one letter off a scheme word ('luôn' ≈ 'Lương …', 'lẹ' / 'lễ' ≈ 'Bán lẻ') leave the period and become the scheme
broken.why: Repros, current tree vs HEAD. (1) On the test file's own fixture, 'Chạy lương tháng 5 luôn cho Payai Retail End-Month chỉ Vũ Khánh Chi': at HEAD it is ready (Payai Retail End-Month + Vũ Khánh Chi). Now the scheme silently becomes Payai Lương khối văn phòng and the people become 'Payai Retail End-Month, Vũ Khánh Chi', so it is refused: 'I could not find "Payai Retail End-Month" among the people…'. (2) 'Chạy lương tháng 5 luôn cho Bán lẻ chỉ Mai', '… cho Bán lẻ, riêng Mai', '… cho Bán lẻ với Mai' and '… cho Bán lẻ cho Mai thôi' (the same with Tính lương / Làm lương / Chạy bảng lương / chay luong / Tạo kỳ lương) are ready at HEAD and refused now, with Bán lẻ read as a person. (3) 'Chạy lương tháng 5 luôn cho Vận tải chỉ Vũ Khánh Chi' is ready at HEAD. Now it asks a scheme question, and the people silently gain Nguyễn Văn Tài (from 'Vận tải'). (4) 'Chạy lương tháng 5 lẹ' ('quickly'), 'Chạy lương tháng 5 lẹ giùm' and 'Chạy lương lễ tháng 5' ('holiday pay') ask which scheme at HEAD; now they silently pick Bán lẻ. Cause: _words_to_move and the span search use _covers_scheme, which accepts near spellings on folded words and ignores the marks. One common filler word therefore counts as a scheme. _names_somebody already refuses a marked word that does not match the name's own marks. Suggested narrowing: in _period_words_to_scheme/_words_to_move, accept only an exact scheme match (_covers_scheme(..., whole=True), or no near-spelling for single words), and refuse a marked word whose marks differ from the scheme's.

broken.item: regression (crit-4 cancel words, runner.py _CANCEL_DONT / _CANCEL_LEAD_VI): a reject or send-back reason that AGREES with the decision now cancels it
broken.why: Stub run on the current runner.py (scratchpad/vr/h2.py). While the turn-down reason is asked for on 'Reject Lan's overtime request': cancel_words("Don't approve it") is True, and so are "Don't approve the overtime" and 'Do not approve this request'. On 'Từ chối yêu cầu tăng ca của Huy': 'Không duyệt tăng ca của Huy' and 'Không duyệt yêu cầu này' are also True. typed_answer() then calls cancel() and the reject is dropped. At HEAD there were no cancel words: each of these is 6 or more characters, so it was stored as the reason and the plan card was shown. On a send-back or turn-down question, 'don't approve' / 'không duyệt' says the same thing as the decision, so it is not a cancel. It is a cancel only on the optional Note question of approve_item. Narrowest fix: accept the approve verb in _CANCEL_DONT ('approve') and 'khong duyet' in _CANCEL_LEAD_VI only when the open task's action is approve_item, or drop both. No existing test asserts that these cancel. The only 'không duyệt' rows in the tests are the 'Huy không duyệt' / 'Khoi không duyệt' must-NOT-cancel rows, which stay as they are. Everything else checked is fixed. only_thanks no longer swallows 'Hiếu đã vắng', 'Vắng nhiều quá', 'Vắng rồi', 'anh Hiếu', 'Chị Tốt' or 'Cấm' (r_thanks7.py: bad 0, plus about 120 more EN/VI phrases in scratchpad/vr/hunt.py with no false thanks). A name typed without marks, such as 'Huy không duyệt' or 'Huy từ chối', does not cancel. People and Scheme questions send 'Huy', 'Dung Nguyen' and 'Thoi' to the lookup again, as at HEAD (rr_pencil.py). The crit4 tables pass (rr_tables.py: 137 checks, 0 bad). wf-10 stub: HEAD shows the English label, the current tree shows the translated one, and an untranslated state falls back to English. sec-4 stub: approve, send back and reject return (False, 'screen_off') when the Home entry or its section is locked. Remind re-asks gate.allowed when pressed. G-cross: runner.py:1442 now reads T(_lt('the word')).

broken.item: regression (vi-10 count words, resolve._VI_REL / _VI_COUNT_WORDS): 'từ' (from) is read as the count 'tư' (four), so 'từ tháng trước / từ tháng sau' lands four months away
broken.why: Stub run, today 13 Oct 2026. parse_period / resolve_period('từ tháng trước') gives June 2026; HEAD gave Sep 2026. 'từ tháng sau' and 'từ tháng tới' give Feb 2027; HEAD gave Nov 2026. Unmarked 'tu thang truoc' gives June too. What this breaks: 'chạy lương từ tháng trước' (run_payroll period), 'gửi phiếu lương từ tháng trước' (send_payslips run), 'xem bảng lương từ tháng trước' (run_status), and the Approvals search for 'duyệt tăng ca từ tháng trước của Lan' or 'trả lại yêu cầu tăng ca từ tháng trước vì sai giờ' (item_query searches June instead of September). parse_day('kể từ tháng sau' / 'bắt đầu từ tháng sau' / 'áp dụng từ tháng sau') gives 1 Feb 2027 (HEAD 1 Nov 2026). The update_pay_data phrase removes 'từ' itself, so the from-date of a pay change is safe. The same fold collision affects 'bà tháng trước' (now 3 months back, July) and 'sau tháng trước' (now 6 back, April). Cause: _VI_REL runs on the folded text, and 'tu', 'ba', 'sau' are in _VI_COUNT_WORDS. Narrow fix: take 'tu' out of the count words (people say 'bốn' for a count of four). In a message that has marks, accept 'ba' / 'sáu' / 'năm' only when written with those marks (not 'bà', 'sau'). The FIX-1 tables stay green: 'ba tháng tới', 'năm tháng trước', 'mười hai tháng trước' and '6 tháng trước' are all written as counts.

broken.item: regression (vi-10 count reading, resolve._not_a_count): a number that labels a run, week or quarter, or the 'năm' (year) in 'cuối năm', is read as a count of months
broken.why: Stub run, today 13 Oct 2026. 'gửi phiếu lương đợt 2 tháng trước' (round 2 of last month), 'duyệt bảng lương đợt 2 tháng trước', 'xem bảng lương kỳ 2 tháng trước', 'chạy lương khối 2 tháng trước' and 'duyệt tăng ca tuần 2 tháng trước' now give Aug 2026 (HEAD Sep 2026). 'chạy lương đợt 2 tháng sau' gives Dec (HEAD Nov). 'duyệt thưởng quý 3 tháng trước' gives July (HEAD Sep). 'duyệt thưởng cuối năm tháng trước' (last month's year-end bonus) and 'duyệt nghỉ phép đầu năm tháng trước' give May 2026 (HEAD Sep 2026), and 'nam' drops out of the Approvals search words. 'duyệt bảng lương giữa năm tháng sau' gives Mar 2027 (HEAD Nov 2026). Narrow fix in _not_a_count: the number is not a count when the word before it is a label (đợt, kỳ, lần, khối, tuần, quý, ca, tổ, nhóm). 'năm' is not a count after cuối / đầu / giữa / cả / mỗi / hằng / hàng. This is the same kind of rule as the existing ngày / mùng one.

broken.item: regression (vi-9, phrases_vi send_back_item pattern 1): 'trả lại X' now needs X to start with a word from _ITEM_WORDS, so many ordinary send-backs match nothing
broken.why: Stub run. Now None, and at HEAD send_back_item: 'trả lại lương tháng 6 vì sai' (HEAD item 'lương tháng 6', reason 'sai'; the Red search ['luong'] for June finds the June run), 'trả lại tháng 6 vì sai', 'trả lại đợt tháng 6', 'trả lại kỳ tháng 6', 'trả lại đợt chạy lương tháng 6', 'trả lại lần chạy lương tháng 6', 'trả lại bảng tính lương tháng 6', 'trả lại payroll tháng 6', 'trả lại pay run tháng 6', 'trả lại Lan', 'trả lại của Lan', 'trả lại cho Mai', 'trả lại cho Mai vì sai', 'gửi trả lại cho Mai', 'trả về cho Mai sửa'. vi-9's own repro needs only two things: 'trả X lại/về' (pattern 2: 'trả lương về', 'trả lời lại') to name a waiting item, and the refund 'trả lại tiền thừa cho Linh' refused. The finding's fix itself scoped the item-word rule to 'trả X lại/về'. Narrow fix: keep _ITEM_WORDS on pattern 2 only. On pattern 1, go back to the HEAD item shape and add a refund lookahead such as (?!\s*tiền\b). The test_vi9 table stays green: 'trả lời lại cho Linh' never matches 'trả lại', and 'trả lương về' is pattern 2.

broken.item: regression (vi-1 third pass, registry._ends_on_particle): an order ending in the emphatic '… đi chứ' / '… đi nhỉ' is now taken as a question
broken.why: Stub run. 'chạy lương tháng 6 đi chứ' (go on, run June payroll) was run_payroll at HEAD (period resolves to June). Now it gives None with looks_like_question True, so it is answered as a question and the plan never starts. The same happens to 'gửi phiếu lương tháng 6 đi chứ', 'duyệt bảng lương tháng 6 đi chứ', 'duyệt đi chứ', 'duyệt luôn đi chứ', 'chạy lương tháng 6 đi nhỉ' and 'duyệt nghỉ phép của Lan đi à' (HEAD approve_item, item 'nghỉ phép của Lan'). 'chứ' and 'nhỉ' were added to _PARTICLES_MARKED beyond vi-1's own repro, which had only 'hả' and 'sao'. Narrow fix: a particle right after 'đi' (or after a polite tail that normalise_vi cuts) is emphasis, not a question. Bare '… chứ' / '… nhỉ' with no 'đi' can stay a question.

broken.item: regression (vi-4 / _TAIL_VI fourth pass, resolve.drop_vi_filler): ANY capital after the first word now counts as a name, so a capitalised filler word ('Mình', 'Đang', 'Đó') becomes a required search word
broken.why: Stub run. resolve_run narrowing words: 'Gửi Phiếu Lương Tháng 6 Của Mình' and 'Gửi phiếu lương tháng 6 Của Mình' give ['minh'] (HEAD []), so the person gets 'I found pay runs for June 2026, but none matching "minh"'. 'Xem Bảng Lương Tháng 6 Đang Chờ' gives ['dang'] (HEAD []). Approvals search: 'Duyệt Cái Đó' gives ['do'], 'Duyệt Yêu Cầu Của Mình' gives ['minh'] and 'Duyệt Yêu Cầu Đang Chờ' gives ['dang']. At HEAD all three gave [] (whatever is waiting for me). The rule was added for Bạn / Thôi / Luôn, where the name is spelled exactly like the little word. For mình / đang / đó the name has its own spelling (Minh, Đặng, Đỗ), so the marks already decide. Narrow fix: apply the capital-is-a-name rule only to words in _NAME_AFTER_CUA (ban, thoi, luon). The tests still pass: 'Đang chờ của mình' is first-word, and the Bạn / Thôi / Luôn rows are unchanged.

broken.item: regression (vi-11 fourth pass, registry._before_reason / _DECIDES_VI): a question about a decide word written with ':' or ' - ' becomes a decision with the reason 'là gì'
broken.why: Stub run. HEAD read these as questions (match None, looks_like_question True). Now 'duyệt: là gì' and 'duyet - la gi' give approve_item {reason: 'là gì'} with question False. 'từ chối: nghĩa là gì' gives reject_item {reason: 'nghĩa là gì'}, 'trả lại - nghĩa là gì' gives send_back_item {reason: 'nghĩa là gì'}, and 'duyệt - là gì' gives approve_item. later: 'duyệt yêu cầu của Lan à' gave approve_item at HEAD and is now treated as a question. This is deliberate: the third pass added the bare question word 'à' as part of vi-1, and a final 'à' usually asks. Treating it as a question can only lose a plan card, never start a decision. Left as is, flagged for the owner's language check.

'15 tháng sau' is now read as 15 months from now (1 Jan 2028); HEAD gave 1 Nov 2026. HEAD was wrong either way, and the words can mean either reading ('ngày 15 tháng sau' gives 15 Nov 2026). Not chased under the convergence rule.

'15 tháng sáu' and '2 tháng 6' (June dates with no year, now in the past) are asked instead of taken as said. This is the P4 crit-3 design: a past date with no year is asked. HEAD gave a wrong date (1 Nov 2026 for the first).

broken.item: FIX-1b:3 regression — an order followed by '… so/and/, <person> can/will approve or sign off for me' is now refused
broken.why: The fourth/sixth-pass pattern in NeverAccess.phrases (the one starting ^(?:.*?(?:[,;:—]|\b(?:so|and|then))\s+)?(?:have\s+)?_SUBJECT(?P<who>…)) allows ANY text before the comma or 'so/and/then', including a whole order. These had an action at HEAD and now get the never card: 'approve the June run so Lan can sign off for me', 'approve the June run, Lan will sign off for me', 'approve the June run and Lan will sign off for me', 'approve the June run, then Lan signs off for me', 'approve the June run and then Minh will sign off for us' (approve_item at HEAD), 'reject the June run so Lan can approve for me' (reject_item), 'send back the June run so Lan can approve for me' (send_back_item), 'show the June run so Lan can approve for me' (run_status), and "approve Lan's payslip so she can sign for me" (approve_item, with who='she', which is plainly signing the payslip). Bare 'sign' with no 'off' also counts: 'Lan will sign the contract for me' and 'Minh will sign the payslips for me' (None at HEAD) now get the never card. Suggested narrowing, not done: the text before the comma must not start with an order verb (for example only an 'I'm / I am / we're / I will be …' statement), and 'sign' should count only as 'sign off'. The original repros still need to pass: "I'm going on leave, Lan will approve for me" and "I'm away next week so Lan will approve for me".

broken.item: FIX-1b:3 regression — a joining word is taken as the person: 'so / and / then … approve … for me'
broken.why: Same pattern. _SUBJECT does not exclude 'so', 'and', 'then', 'ok', 'just', 'also' or 'now', so a plain approval with a lead-in word becomes a hand-over to a person called 'so'. These were None at HEAD (an approval request for the model) and now get the never card, with who='so' / 'ok so' / 'and' / 'then': 'so approve the June run for me', 'ok so approve the June run for me', 'and approve the June run for me', 'then approve the June run for me', "I'm away, so approve the June run for me", "it's late, so approve it for me". Without the lead-in, 'approve the June run for me' still gives approve_item. Adding the joining words to the _SUBJECT negative lookahead should close it.
